advisory.finding: `test_internal_callers_use_the_silent_impl` asserts by grepping each module's source text (`assert "_review_ticket_impl" in src`) rather than exercising behavior, contradicting its own docstring ('Asserted on the resolved call target, not on source text'). It is a source-grep of the code under test: it passes if the token appears anywhere (an import, a comment, a docstring, or an unrelated line) and breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. import aliasing), while NOT detecting a regression where a module also still mentions the token but actually calls the warning wrapper.
merged_from: The 'internal callers must not double-signal the deprecation' contract has behavioral regression coverage ONLY for the MCP path (test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal). The two other in-source callers named as must-not-warn — review_workflows.py (diff_review_paths legacy leg) and evals/eval_solver.py — have no test that actually executes them and asserts absence of a DeprecationWarning; their contract is 'covered' solely by the source-grep in test_internal_callers_use_the_silent_impl.
scenarios: A future refactor renames or wraps the internal call; the grep still passes though the resolved target changed.
A module's body reverts to calling `review_ticket` (double-warn) while still importing/mentioning `_review_ticket_impl`; the grep passes and the regression is missed.
advisory.suggested_fix: For review_workflows (via diff_review_paths) and eval_solver, invoke the caller under `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)` with a FakeRunner injected and assert zero DeprecationWarnings — mirroring test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal — instead of reading module source text.
